newsitem.title: UK: Sterling/mark boosted by French election result.
newsitem.headline: Sterling/mark boosted by French election result.

text.p: Sterling/mark was at three-and-a-half week highs at mid-session Europe, boosted by worries about a soft euro after the Socialist Party won parliamentary elections in France.
Sterling's strength was further enhanced by the UK May purchasing output managers' index which, at 58.1 versus 56.7 in April, showed the highest growth rate since September 1996.
"Sterling has benefitted from the French election result as a currency aloof from the EMU process," said Paul Lambert, senior currency strategist at UBS here.
Sterling was at 2.8153/63 marks at 1230 GMT compared to 2.7960/75 late on Friday. Cable was at $1.6358/68 versus $1.6360/70.

The market also fed on final M4 money supply figures showing a rise of 10.2 percent in the year to April versus a forecast 10.4 percent. M0 rose a provisional 6.1 percent in the year to May versus a forecast 6.0 percent.
And sterling/mark was further bolstered by strength in dollar/mark.
"The correlation between sterling/mark and dollar/mark has also benefitted sterling on the European crosses," said Lambert.
But analysts agreed the main driving force behind sterling's rise was the Socialist Party victory in France, which has heightened worries of a softer euro.
The Socialist Party has said it would be "masochistic" to try to meet the Maastricht guidelines and is more concerned with getting France's army of unemployed back to work.
"Regardless of the euro-friendly noises that the UK government is making, sterling is still being seen as a safe-haven," said Dharshini David, UK economist at HSBC markets.
